title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to evaluate whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents drawn from a deterministic generator, execution semantic = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per intent reused across conditions), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, guarded pipeline allowed ≤1 repair. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (≈0.67 pp); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate estimand and a one-repair budget the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over an already near-ceiling baseline. We report (a) the artifact-backed numerical outcome, (b) an explicit mapping between the originally preregistered three-condition hypothesis labeling and the actually executed paired contrast, and (c) methodological recommendations—notably baseline-calibration pilots—because the observed baseline invalidated the preregistered power assumption.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by converting free-text operator intents into executable device configurations. Prior work reports that single-pass LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, omissions, or sequencing mistakes that violate safety or availability invariants and therefore motivates generate→verify→repair pipelines that pair generation with deterministic verification or repair [1][2][3]. Our preregistered confirmatory question was narrowly stated after an autonomous literature review: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? We preregistered study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and froze the analysis plan before observing any model outputs. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, artifactized paired trial on a deterministic synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents) using strict shared_initial_candidate execution semantics; (2) artifact-grounded numeric outcomes showing baseline = 149/150 and guarded = 150/150 with accompanying inferential diagnostics; (3) a methods clarification that maps preregistered hypothesis labels to the executed contrasts and an operational recommendation—baseline-calibration pilots—because the observed ceiling effect invalidated the preregistered power assumptions.
sections.related_work: Research on NL→configuration translation, verifier-guided repair, and agentic LLM safety motivates our design. Studies of intent translation and intent-driven configuration report that free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants; reported semantic-correctness rates vary and often remain modest depending on task heterogeneity and oracle choice [2][4]. Work integrating deterministic verifiers into generation workflows (TerraFormer-style verifier feedback, generate→verify→repair pipelines) reports practical correctness gains for IaC and configuration-repair tasks, but effect sizes depend on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, repair budget, and sampling semantics [5][6]. Formal network-verification tooling (NetKAT/KATch and related systems) provides deterministic oracles for reachability and isolation checks but varies in supported abstractions and scale [7]. Security analyses show that unguarded agentic tool orchestration can convert false textual claims into harmful actions, motivating conservative verifier gating and auditable verdicts [8]. Our study differs from many prior evaluations by (a) enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial sampled candidate was reused across conditions for each intent), (b) constraining the repair budget to ≤1 repair, and (c) using a deterministic verifier as the binary confirmatory oracle. These choices make our primary estimand the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to a fixed first-pass candidate rather than the difference between independently sampled pipelines.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design summary. The trial was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and frozen prior to any model calls. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on deterministic-verifier pass/fail. Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access, VLAN/MTU sequences, uplink switchover). The preregistered power plan targeted a detectable +15 percentage-point absolute improvement with N≈150 (conservative discordant assumptions). Inclusion/exclusion rules, ambiguity detection, mapping unit-tests, retry policy (one retry for provider timeouts), and multiplicity corrections were defined and archived in the preregistration.

Explicit mapping from preregistration labels to executed contrasts (reviewer-requested clarification). The preregistration conceptually described three conditions: A = baseline (free-text), B = constrained template prompting, C = constrained + verifier-feedback (guarded). In the archived run the execution adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and a single initial generation per intent that was reused across conditions; therefore the confirmatory estimand executed and archived is the marginal guarded (C) vs baseline (A) contrast computed on the identical sampled initial candidate for each intent. Constrained-only (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition under independent sampling in this run and therefore no independent B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts are reported from the archived artifacts. The preregistered H1/H2 labels (H1: constrained vs baseline; H2: guarded vs constrained) remain in the preregistration record but the actually tested primary contrast in the archived execution is C vs A with shared_initial_candidate semantics; this mapping is explicit here and in the Disclosure Statement. No post-preregistration changes to the confirmatory analysis were performed: the analysis in artifacts follows the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.

Execution adapter semantics, model, and deterministic validator. The adapter enforced the following at runtime and recorded provider accounting: exactly one initial model generation per intent (shared_initial_generation = 150) and at most one additional repair call permitted only when the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate (repair invocations = 1). Declared model in execution metadata: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The recorded model_configuration.json declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied the archived full_intent_constraint_validation rule; the validator returned a boolean pass/fail verdict plus normalized_configuration text and per-episode diagnostics. These deterministic verdicts formed the binary endpoint used in the confirmatory McNemar test.

Task generation, mapping tests, and contamination controls. Tasks were produced deterministically with generator seeds archived; topologies were constrained to small verifier-capable networks (4–32 nodes). Parser and mapping unit-tests that transform textual outputs to verifier inputs were executed prior to batch evaluation and passed. The adapter executed contamination checks (session isolation, duplicate-response detection); all checks passed and contamination_summary.csv is empty. Planned episodes = 300 (150 intents × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 300 and complete pairs = 150 in the execution manifest.

Statistical analysis. The primary test used exact two-sided McNemar on the paired contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00). We reported absolute percentage-point differences, exact p-values, and a 95% bootstrap percentile CI computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered handling of incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary) excluded incomplete pairs from primary inference; no incomplete pairs occurred in the archived run. Secondary contrasts and multiplicity corrections were preregistered but were not executed as independent-condition comparisons given the adapter-enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and recorded stage counts (see Results). All analysis scripts and artifacts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider accounting (artifact-grounded): model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151; stage_counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 1. No contamination flags or pre-execution unit-test failures occurred.

Primary numerical outcomes. Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These numbers are reported verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and revision counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150). That single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces (validation_before, validation_after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes) are archived for every episode; representative traces for tasks 000001–000006 illustrate typical difficulty patterns and the validator’s diagnostic outputs.

Representative artifact-grounded example. Task-000001 (generator_seed = 1) intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial response and both condition responses matched the preregistered expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics for task-000001: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. The shared-initial candidate SHA-256 and normalized_configuration strings are archived in the execution bundle.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred; contamination_summary.csv is empty.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect, power, and inferential consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline and targeted detection of an absolute +15 pp improvement. The observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left virtually no headroom for improvement: with n_11 = 149 and only a single discordant pair (n_10 = 1), the paired analysis provides little discordant information and the planned power assumptions no longer hold. Put plainly, the trial’s preregistered detectable-effect assumptions were invalidated by the observed near-ceiling baseline, and the exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI containing zero reflect that fact. We therefore recommend that preregistered NetOps trials include a short baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks sampled from the planned generator and prompt style) to estimate baseline competence and adjust confirmatory N or task difficulty before committing to final sampling.

Why baseline was high on the synthetic corpus. The deterministic task generator produced intents that were often tightly specified (explicit required_sequence, constrained allowed_fields), and the verifier coverage matched the required invariants for the small topologies used. In such circumstances a capable LLM frequently yields a verifier-satisfying candidate on a single draw; the artifact traces (tasks 000001–000006) show fully specified sequences and constrained action spaces that reduce translation ambiguity and therefore raise baseline success.

Sampling semantics, estimand interpretation, and operational trade-offs. The enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolated the marginal effect of applying a repair to an identical first-pass candidate. Alternative semantics—independent per-condition sampling or multi-draw ensembles—estimate different operational questions (expected pass rates under independent draws, or the effect of repeated repairs) and often increase discordant-pair counts (n_10 + n_01) at the cost of additional model calls and latency. Practitioners must align experimental semantics with deployment constraints (whether systems resample or must act on a single first-pass candidate) and include model-call cost in power planning.

Operational affordances beyond binary pass/fail. Even when guarded pipelines yield small marginal verifier-pass improvements, deterministic verifier outputs (normalized configurations, explicit violation codes, parsed_command_count) provide operational observability that supports auditable triage and targeted human repair. Our archival traces illustrate concrete diagnostic categories (missing step, order violation) that are valuable in practice even if the binary pass/fail rate changes little on a constrained corpus.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the adapter-enforced call budgets, contamination checks, and mapping unit-tests mitigate many internal threats; no deviations from the preregistration were recorded. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is only as faithful as the mapping code and verifier coverage; uncovered mapping or coverage gaps would bias measured semantic correctness. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic small topologies (4–32 nodes); results should not be extrapolated to larger networks, other models, or vendor-specific CLI heterogeneity. Security: adversarial prompt-injection and claim-to-action attacks were not evaluated and remain separate concerns requiring adversary-driven studies.

Practical prescriptions. Based on artifact-grounded outcomes we recommend: (1) baseline-calibration pilots to estimate baseline_success_rate before confirmatory sampling; (2) explicit preregistration of generation semantics and repair budgets; (3) multi-arm designs that vary repair budgets and sampling semantics to estimate cost–benefit frontiers; (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power and cost planning; (5) staged scaling of verifier coverage and topology size with deterministic mapping unit-tests. The archived execution manifest and task seeds permit reproducible pilots and multi-arm follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial under strict shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing baseline free-text prompting versus constrained prompting plus a one-repair deterministic verifier loop. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The primary scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate power planning. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness (149/150 ≈ 99.33%) was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
